title: Enterprise E-commerce Platform
tagline: From building the product detail page to leading its team and client
summary: A large US home-furnishings e-commerce platform. For the first year I built the Product Detail Page hands-on: the PDP V2 architecture, configurator options and the start of PDP V3 behind feature flags. Since then I have led the work: training and supporting a junior developer, reviewing code and handling client communication.
overview: A large-scale e-commerce platform for a US home-furnishings retailer, with a customer storefront and a Concierge app that in-store sales associates use. My focus was the Product Detail Page, the page where customers configure and buy.

In my first year (Jul 2023 – mid 2024) I coded hands-on: I set up the ProductV2 architecture that later PDP versions build on, added configurator options, split a heavy GraphQL query to speed up product cards, and started PDP V3 behind feature flags.

After that a junior developer took over day-to-day coding. I trained them on the codebase, review their code, and run the client side: requirement meetings, technical discussions and planning the project work.
statsNote: From git history and my role on the project.

points: Set up the ProductV2 architecture for the PDP rebuild, the base that later PDP versions build on.
Built a pagination component for product grids and added configurator options to the new PDP.
Started the PDP V3 work behind feature flags for safe rollouts: swatches, add-swatch-to-cart and surcharge messaging.
Split a heavy product line-item GraphQL query into fragments and reworked related-product cards so they load faster.
Trained a junior developer on the codebase and support them with implementation.
Review code to keep it in line with project standards.
Handle client communication: requirement meetings, technical discussions and project planning.

achievements: Laid the ProductV2 foundation that later PDP versions build on.
Grew from hands-on PDP engineer to leading the team and the client relationship.
Trained the developer who now builds PDP features day to day.
